title: Brown founds NICAP; Hillenkoetter on board

tellings.quote: When Brown returned from the International Geophysical Year, he created NICAP, or the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena.
realize that he started NICAP, which was the first civilian UFO tracking program in 1956.
tellings.difference: Calls it the first civilian UFO tracking program and does not mention Hillenkoetter or the International Geophysical Year.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Townsend Brown founding NICAP, the civilian UFO group, in 1956.

plain: An American inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have founded NICAP, the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena, in 1956, a civilian group set up to track and study UFO reports. Michels tells this himself in two episodes. In a documentary about Brown, he says Brown created it after returning from the International Geophysical Year, a worldwide scientific effort of that era, and he names a former head of the CIA, Roscoe Hillenkoetter, as one of the people tied to the group. In another episode he calls NICAP the first civilian UFO tracking program and leaves out Hillenkoetter. It matters to him because it would link a secretive government scientist and a former spy chief to the earliest public UFO research.
